title: Signs He Likes You: What to Look For and How to Be Sure — cv.cm
description: Signs he likes you, in person and in messages: what each sign may mean, how sure you can be, and how to find out with one small, honest step.
h1: How do you know if he likes you?
answer: He probably likes you if he makes steady effort over weeks: he starts contact, remembers what you said, makes time to see you, looks for reasons to be near you and asks about your life. One sign proves little; a pattern says more. The clearest way to know is a small invitation or a kind, direct question.

sections.h: The short version: look for effort, not a single clue
body: This page says "he" because that is what people search, but the signs are not male. People of any gender show interest in much the same ways, and they also differ a lot from person to person. A quiet man and a loud man, or a man from Seoul and a man from Madrid, may show the same feeling very differently. Read the signs below as clues about one person, not rules about men.

The most useful idea is effort over time. Anyone can be friendly once. Someone who likes you keeps choosing you: he comes back to talk, he follows up, and he makes plans that actually happen. Research on attraction finds that people tend to like those who show they like them, partly because shown interest signals good intentions. So the warmth you see is real information, but it needs to repeat before it means much.

Be careful with your own reading too. Studies of first meetings find that people misjudge interest in both directions: some people see interest that is not there, and others miss interest that is. A sign is a reason to look closer, not proof.

body: Body language is real but weak. In one small speed-dating study, the way two people's movements followed each other was linked to long-term interest, but that kind of signal is subtle and hard to see with the eye. Do not build a conclusion on eye contact or posture alone.

sections.h: Signs he likes you over messages
body: Messages give you a record, which helps, but they also hide tone. Signs that tend to matter:

ul: He starts the conversation at least some of the time, not only you.
He asks questions back and picks up on what you said yesterday.
His replies are about as long and as warm as yours.
He sends things that made him think of you: a song, a photo, a place.
He suggests a call or a meeting instead of only chatting.

body: Reply speed alone means little. People have jobs, classes, family and different habits with their phone. A slow but thoughtful reply is a better sign than a fast "lol". For a full guide, see the article on signs someone likes you over text.

sections.h: Shy guys, confident guys, and just being friendly
body: A shy man who likes you may talk less, not more. He may look away when you catch his eye, reply carefully, and rarely make the first move. The signs are small but steady: he stays near, he remembers, he shows up. A confident man may be direct and fast, which is clear, but confident people are sometimes warm with everyone.
The key question is: does he treat you differently from other people? This table helps separate friendly from interested.

sections.h: Signs he likes you but is holding back
body: Sometimes the signs are there but nothing moves. Common reasons, and what you can do:

ul: He is afraid of rejection. Make a small, easy opening, like a shared plan, so he does not have to risk a big step alone.
He does not want to lose a friendship. A calm, private talk can lower the stakes for both of you.
You work or study together. He may worry about awkwardness or rules. Respect that; any step should be private and easy to decline.
He has just left a relationship or is going through a hard time. Interest may be real but not ready.
He is waiting for a clear moment. In places where confessing feelings is a normal step, such as Japan, Korea, China and Taiwan, some people hold back until they feel sure enough to confess.
He is not that interested, or he is keeping his options open. If a long time passes and he never moves closer, treat that as an answer.

body: If he is warm one week and distant the next, that is a different pattern. See the article on mixed signals.

sections.h: How to find out if he likes you
body: Guessing for months costs more than one honest step. You have two good options.

ol: Make a small invitation. Choose something specific and low-pressure: "I'm going to that new noodle place on Friday after class. Want to come?" If he says yes and shows up, that is real information. If he says "Maybe another time" and never offers another time, that is also information.
Ask kindly and directly, in private. "I like spending time with you, and I wanted to ask: do you see me as a friend, or as something more?" Keep it short and let him answer.
If he needs time, give it: "No pressure. Take your time." Then do not chase.
Accept the answer. A yes is a start. A no or a vague answer means stop pushing and go back to normal, kind behavior.

body: In East Asia many people still date after a clear confession, and in many Western places people go on dates first and talk about the relationship later. Either path is fine. What matters is that you both say what you want at some point. If you want to go further, see the articles on how to ask someone out and how to confess your feelings. cv.cm's Does my crush like me test can also help you sort through what you have seen.

sections.h: Mistakes to avoid and when to stop

ul: Do not test him with games, like making him jealous or ignoring him to see if he chases. It confuses both of you and teaches nothing true.
Do not read his phone, check who he follows, or ask his friends to spy. Ask him.
Do not wait forever. If months pass with no step from him after you have made an opening, it is fair to move on.
Do not ignore your own feelings. The question is not only "does he like me?" but also "do I enjoy how he treats me?"
Do not explain away a clear no. "I'm not looking for anything right now" means exactly that for now.

body.note: A good rule: watch what he does over several weeks, not what he says in one moment. Effort that keeps coming is the most honest sign there is.

faq.q: How do you know if a guy likes you but is hiding it?
faq.a: Look for small, steady signs: he stays near you, remembers details, and shows up when you invite him, even if he says little. Make one easy opening, like a specific plan, and see if he takes it.

faq.q: Does a lot of eye contact mean he likes you?
faq.a: It can, but eye contact also depends on personality and culture, and some people look away when they like someone. Treat it as a weak sign and look for effort and plans as well.

faq.q: How long does it take a guy to show he likes you?
faq.a: There is no fixed time. Many people show some interest within a few meetings or weeks of chatting. If months pass with no step closer after you have made an opening, he is probably not ready or not interested.

faq.q: Can he like me if he does not text much?
faq.a: Yes. Some people dislike texting but show interest in person by making time and keeping plans. What matters is whether he puts effort into you somewhere, not only in chat.

faq.q: Should I just ask him if he likes me?
faq.a: Often, yes. A short, private and calm question saves weeks of guessing. Make it easy to answer either way, and accept what he says.
